proposals.relationship: Owram praises Parr’s individual studies but questions whether Domestic Goods sustains a coherent argument about consumer sovereignty and the rationality of Canadian choices.
proposals.evidence_note: Own2001 review103–105: distinguishes the restricted postwar market from later choices and consumers collectively from individual consumers. He credits Parr’s modernist-design and material-culture studies; disagreement is particular, not rejection of her work. The complete book remains unread.
primary_locators: BC Studies129(Spring2001),103–105, own review ending with the Ford/Volvo comparison; next review on105 excluded.

proposals.relationship: As Buckner reconstructs the1997 argument, Owram calls for studying how regional and local identities interact within a shared national experience while rejecting a return to a patriotic elite’s master narrative.
proposals.evidence_note: Explicit Buckner2000 mediation, paragraphs10–15 and notes18/19. Buckner disputes Owram’s equation of regional study with overspecialization and qualifies common-law/social-program claims, while accepting his concluding focus on identity interplay. The original Narrow Circles remains unread. Do not collapse this position into Bliss’s or Granatstein’s.
primary_locators: Buckner, Limited Identities Revisited, printed9–12, especially Owram quotation and reply, notes18/19;1997 original11,17–18 cited by the reader.
